header.description: Boundless DAS (Wu et al. 2023, arXiv 2305.08809): das.json's rotation widened to k = 64 with a boundary gate behind it, so the fit learns its own rank instead of sweeping k. `bnd` has ONE parameter theta in [0, 1], the boundary as a fraction of the rotation's 64 ordered columns (beta = 64 theta): the training mask is sigmoid((beta - i) / T) over the column index i, the eval mask keeps the first ceil(beta) columns, and the l1 term is the kept fraction (the paper's boundary-width penalty, weight 1.0 as in Wu et al.) - so ce pulls beta up, l1 pulls it down, and a column stays kept while it lowers ce by more than lambda / k = 1/64 nats; 0.05 would hold nothing against ce at this width. The boundary trains at lr 1e-2, ten times the rotation's (pyvene's recipe): at the rotation's 1e-3 an Adam step moves theta by ~0.001 of the width per update and the boundary barely leaves its start while the rotation fills whatever prefix is open. The temperature anneals 1.0 -> 0.1 over the WHOLE run, not to 0.01 by mid-run: below ~0.1 the sigmoid's gradient is a spike narrower than one column and the boundary freezes wherever it stands. The start is the default theta = 1/2, beta = 32 (fill 1/2). k is the width the boundary may reach, not the rank claimed. fit_diagnostics.json records `boundary` (beta) and `hard_mask_size` (the learned rank) beside the rotation's orthonormality, so a report can place this fit on the IIA-vs-k curve of weekdays_das_sweep.json as one point. The size-matched control is random_subspace_control.json with k set to the learned rank. Everything else is das.json.
